limits: Four synthetic coding prompts with 256-token output caps; Fibonacci stops at 95 tokens.
The two comparisons are separate ABBA experiments; their rates should not be mixed into a single round.
No continuous quietness trace. Thermal state was sampled at round boundaries; every round waited for nominal state before warmup, and some ended fair.
The four-concurrent comparison includes prefill, queueing and decode; above 5% ABBA spread is inconclusive.
The CPU reference and serving checks cover finite cases; different FP32 reduction order can move near ties on other inputs.

reproduction.command: python -m dev.benchmarks.draft_comparison --baseline-binary BASELINE/splash --candidate-binary CANDIDATE/splash --baseline-model-root BASELINE_MODEL_ROOT --candidate-model-root DSPINE_MODEL_ROOT --output OUTPUT_DIR
reproduction.before_after: Both roots select DSpine; baseline binary/metallib are built from baseline_commit.
reproduction.dflash_vs_optimized: Both binaries/metallibs are the candidate build; the baseline root selects DFlash2.
reproduction.binary_dependencies: Each binary has its own splash.metallib and host-step.metallib beside it.
reproduction.result_metric: ABBA lower-is-better milliseconds per token. Displayed combined rates are 1000 / ABBA mean milliseconds per token.

production_profile.scope: 128-token Roman Empire chat prompt, four cycles per width, 1-4 requests. Fused times and separate-dispatch attribution replays advance decode history independently. This is attribution, not an ABBA throughput comparison.

target_weight_verification.method: The native weight-digests tool loaded both model roots as the engine does and hashed all loaded target images.
target_weight_verification.cache_identity_note: The status target_model_sha256 identifies prepared-image manifests, which differ across these installations despite identical target image bytes. The HTTP harness compares the installed target source digests/configuration; this separate check verifies actual loaded target image bytes.
